name: taskset
description: Sets or retrieves a process's CPU affinity — which cores it may run on.

flags.description: Core list form, e.g. -c 0,2-3 (more readable than hex masks).
Get/set affinity of a running process.
Apply to all threads of the process.

examples.explanation: Pins the benchmark to cores 0–1 for consistent, repeatable measurements.
Shows which cores a running process may use.
Restricts a running process to cores 2–3 — live core isolation for a noisy process.

about: Affinity is a scheduling constraint, not a usage limiter — a process pinned to one core can still use 100% of it. Real resource capping needs cgroups (systemd CPUQuota=) or cpulimit. Pinning helps with cache locality, NUMA placement, and benchmark reproducibility.
useCases: Isolating noisy processes from latency-sensitive ones.
mistakes: Expecting taskset to limit CPU percentage — it only selects cores.
